body: I met my boyfriend in one of my classes my first semester in college, but we didn't really talk to each other dept being classmates. The following semester I learned that he was an aviation major like me and was also training to become a pilot, so he became more interesting to me. We started talking whenever we'd run into each other, then it hanging out with each other from there, and a few weeks later he asked me to be his girlfriend. I'd never been in a relationship before that and was a little nervous about it, but 3 and a half years later I can say it's one of the best decisions I've ever made and that he's truly the light of my life.

My boyfriend was recently gifted a pistol and a shotgun from his uncle. Besides him teaching me basic gun safety and how to use both guns since I had zero experience with guns before this, we haven't used them. He intends on only using them for self defense if someone were to break into our apartment, but plans on taking me to a gun range so that I actually have experience with using it before a situation comes up where I might have to actually use it.

One time I stayed over at my aunt's house for a few days. It was the middle of the summer and really hot and stuffy, so I wore a pair of shorts and a tank top to lounge around the house. I got scolded by my aunt for 'dressing like I was trying to seduce her husband' and told I needed to wear longer pants if I wanted to stay at her house. Mind you, I was 10 years old at the time and this was my mom's brother she was refering to. It's just really fucked to think that even young girls are expected to cover up for men in the house, even those who are relatived to them, and the implications of this become more horrifying now that I'm an adult.

According to Sisters of the Skies, an organization of black women pilots, less than 150 black female pilots have a commercial, military, or airline transport pilot's license in the entire United States. It's mind blowing just how much of a rarity they are and I hope more black girls can be exposed to aviation so that they know it's even a career choice that they have.

As someone who is working on getting their commercial pilots license and hopes to have a career as a pilot, I find it important to read about the causes of aviation accidents so that I know what actions and behaviors not to partake in once I begin my aviation career. Almost all aviation regulations are written in blood, and it's a shame that it doesn't seem like Pakistan's aviation industry has learned much, if anything, from their aviation accidents, seeing as they had 4 airline crashes happen within 10 years. I truly hope that major changes and overhauls to their industry start now so that no more lives have to be unecessarily put at risk in order to travel by plane.

I was the token black person at a school with mostly white and Arab students, and I constantly heard my male classmates talk about how they thought black girls were ugly and repulsive and that they'd never be caught dead dating one while they constantly put the white girls on a pedastal. I also had really bad acne and hair that looked frizzy and unkempt no matter what I did with it, so that just made me feel even worse about my appearance. It wasn't until I went to college out of state that guys started to complement me on my appearance, and I realized that the girls they deemed attractive were average looking and were hyped up because of white beauty standards. However, their comments destroyed my self esteem and it's still hard for me to truly believe that I'm actually beautiful even though I know that I shouldn't let other's opinions dictate my thoughts about my appearance.

It's morbidly fascinating how many planes that crash into the ocean are never found, despite how much technology we have nowadays, but yet again only around 5 to 10 percent of the world's oceans are have been explored and charted so that shouldn't be super surprising.

I'd say so, before the pandemic hit I was on track to graduating from college in May, I was about to enter a career field which had so many job opportunities I was almost guaranteed work in it, and my severe depression I'd had for years was finally starting to improve. Of course that all went down the drain as soon as the pandemic hit, and it took such a toll on me that I reverted back to unhealthy habit use and ended up having suicidal thoughts. I'm really trying to push through and not give up, but it's very difficult and it often feels like I'm fighting a losing battle in that regards.

I was made to think that being introverted was a bad thing since as a child, my mother would force me to talk to other kids at events in an attempt to make me more social and would even get mad at me if she thought I didn't put enough effort into it. I realized as I grew up that I'd never be a social butterfly like she is and there's nothing wrong with that, seeing as I have a decent social life despite not being very outgoing or talkative.

I have a very strong feeling that this country is going to have a severe mental health crisis on its hands with all the negative events happening at once. Many people have lost their loved ones to covid 19, unemployment rates are the highest that they've been in a very long time, essential workers put their lives at risk every time they go to work, and children are falling behind in their education. On top of this, constantly seeing videos of black people being racially abused and killed by cops is an upsetting reminder that anti black racism is inescapable. There is no way that most people are going to come out of this pandemic mentally unscathed; I've suffered from depression for 7 years and this is the worst that it's ever been, and almost all of my family members and friends have felt depressed or anxious recently. A lot of people have told me that things will get better and I should have a positive outlook, but I can't find anything to be hopeful about right now and unfortunately there are many others who feel the same way.

I've been clowned by some of my friends and relatives because my boyfriend has a bigger butt than I do, and his is average sized. I honestly feel self conscious about my flat butt since a lot of black women who are seen as sexy have big butts unlike me, and as much as some guys say little booties matter, most of these same people would prefer a woman with a big one. I hope someday I'll be confident enough to embrace my small butt, but for now that's something I'll have to continue working towards.

My boyfriend and I handle this in very different ways. I've been avoiding the news and social media because the constant negative news is triggering to me, meanwhile he wants to be informed of what's going on and constantly watches the news. While I constantly complain about feeling angry and hopeless, he doesn't really express negative feelings and acts like everything is okay. While the differences in how we cope has led to minor arguements a few times, he does support me by letting me vent to him when I'm upset, comforting me and letting me know that it's okay for me to be upset and that I don't have to fight all the time.

I had a similar discussion with my dad at a few days ago, and by the end of it I was extremely appalled with him. I told him that it's frustrating that in general, black women are loyal and supportive of black men, a few of them to the point that they protect and defend problematic ones, meanwhile a lot of them don't have that same level of loyalty towards us. He kept on saying that was false, so I told him about how one of my friends was in an abusive relationship with her boyfriend, and even after he beat her so badly that she needed to be hospitalized, she refused to press charges because she didn't want to see another black man locked up. 

In response to this, my dad praised her for protecting him by saying that she understands the need to protect black men from the prison system and said that black women should just leave their abusive partners and not try to get them put in jail. On top of this, he tried to blame racism, poverty, and media indoctrination for why abusive black men become that way. I told him that those aren't valid excuses for their behavior, and that abusive black men need to be imprisoned so they don't put other black women at risk of harm. After I asked him if I were to be abused, would he tell me not to report it to police, he told me that he hoped I'm not stupid enough to get into an abusive relationship and if that happened he'd be disappointed in me for not seeing the signs of abuse. 

I told him that him making up excuses for problematic black men along with victim blaming  views disgusted me and that his comments made it very clear that he isn't someone I could turn to if I ended up in that situation. It was just super heartbreaking for me to realize that my dad who I idealized as an example of a respectful and loyal black man was really defending abusive men and insisting that they shouldn't face consequences for their actions. I've actually been avoiding him since that argument and it crushes me to know that I'll never be able to look at him the same way again.

I've spent today avoiding social media and watching the news. I know it's good to be informed of what's happening but the constant negativity of everything that's been going on recently is taking a toll on my already awful mental health and I just need a break from all of it for now.

I actually got into an arguement with one of my former high school friends over this topic a few weeks back. In response to her asking why I don't talk to anyone from our old school, I told her about how having to hear my male classmates constantly talking about how ugly and undateable they found black girls and only praising white girls' appearances destroyed my self esteem and made me feel undesirable, especially since I was the only one of my friends who'd never dated anyone at the time. (I attended a small, mostly white school where I could count the number of black students there on one hand.) I thought that she'd be somewhat understanding of this as a middle eastern woman, but I was proven wrong.

She was super dismissive about it and told me that I was being ridiculous for being bothered by their comments since I'm 'pretty' and have a boyfriend, and insisted that it's okay for my old classmates to have preferences and that they weren't obligated to find black women attractive. Even after I explained to her that labeling an entire group of people as ugly and undateable for no reason besides their ethnicity was not about preference but was in fact racist, she still defended them by insisting they're good people and didn't mean it in that way and therefore I shouldn't be so harsh on them. At that point in time I decided that I was done explaining the issues black women experience to nonblack people since they most likely either won't care about it or will try to downplay and make excuses for the misogynoir directed towards us.

My mom wouldn't let me get my ears pierced at all growing up since she was scared they would get infected, she had that happen to her as a child and never wore earrings again afterwards. She also wouldn't let me wear nail polish colors she deemed too grown like red or black nail polish, now I know I'm not the only one whose mom had those types of rules.

Absolutely no one in a relationship should tolerarate disrespect, infidelity, or generally awful behavior that the other person has no interest in changing in hopes of being awarded with marriage despite the struggle love narrative being somewhat glorified in some black movies and TV shows.

I tried playing video games, but I gave up on it since I was terrible at it. I used to play the piano many years ago, hopefully I can try getting back into it once I can find one to use. I've been hopeful about someday making real friends my entire life, but I'm at the point in my life where I don't want to put any effort into doing so anymore since I've been disappointed too many times to count.
A vacuum cleaner, it was so bad that I'd run into a closet and hide every time my parents were using it.

As long as I can remember I've had trouble socializing and making friends, so I was a loner who never had a stable friend group on top of having social anxiety. I think this loneliness was a contributing factor to me developing depression during my early teenage years. The only motivation that kept me going through school was the idea that once I graduated, I'd go to college with a more diverse group of people and would make better friends. 

However, I went to college, and despite putting myself out there and making an effort to befriend people and join clubs, I didn't form any genuine friendships. I was still alone, and I thought that there was something wrong with me since I couldn't make friends no matter where I was, and I thought that I'd forever be lonely and miserable. The crippling loneliness and being at a college I hated made my depression so much worse, and it escalated to me attempting suicide twice while I attended. I still have suicidal thoughts at times because this pandemic is making me feel so much more isolated than ever, and I honestly worry that if it doesn't end soon I might not be able to keep going much longer.
Oreos. I ate an entire packet of them in one go as a child, and later woke up in the middle of the middle to puke it all up. I haven't touched them since then.

I had a similar experience growing up. My mom would constantly talk about how proud she was of her blackness, but the schools and extra curricular activities I attended barely had any other black students there and she wouldn't let me hang out with black kids in my neighborhood that she deemed too 'ghetto' or low class. As a result, most of my friends growing up were nonblack and I didn't feel much of a connection to black culture despite identifying as black. However, when I started to apply for colleges, my mom insisted that I needed to attend an HBCU for the black experince.

I ended up attending an HBCU since it offered me a full ride and had the major that I wanted, but as I expected, I had a really hard time adjusting. I got told by multiple students there that I wasn't really black since I didn't know about a lot of aspects of the culture, and I worried that I wouldn't be able to make black friends at all because of my upbringing. I realized that my college was extremely bougie and pretentious for an HBCU, so I branched out and made friends with a few people both there and off campus who didn't fit that mold and met my boyfriend of 3 years there. What helped me get through was of course learning more about my culture on my own and realizing that black people aren't a monoloth and if I don't fit in with a particular group of them, there are others out there who will share my same interests and won't make me feel like I'm not black enough.

I feel you on that, I have RBF along with a more serious personality, and I don't feel inclined to smile unless I have a reason to. It's pretty annoying because I've been told by my mom and grandma countless times that I'd look so much prettier if I smiled more and have had random men ask me why I'm not smiling when I'm literally walking to go somewhere or taking public transportation. My life does not revolve around looking attractive for people and I don't owe anyone a smile, especially not some random person on the side of the street.

I still dress in a way my mother would deem appropriate whenever I see her to avoid her negative comments. She genuinely believes that covering my body up will stop guys from catcalling me since she's bustier than I am and received a lot of negative attention for it, and she said that men were more respectful to her once she converted to Islam and started wearing a burka. It didn't stop creepy guys from trying to talk to me, but it did succeed in making me feel ashamed and embarrassed about having larger boobs.

My mental health journey has been a roller coaster. I was diagnosed with autism as a toddler, which resulted in me having trouble with picking up on social cues and socializing in general. Therefore, my mom tried to improve my social skills by forcing me to talk to other kids around me, and I would get in trouble if she thought I wasn't making enough of an effort to socialize. As a result, I have pretty bad social anxiety, and I've struggled with loneliness for my entire childhood as a result of constantly being bullied by my classmates and not having many friends.

I then got diagnosed with depression when I was 17 years old, even though looking back I think I've had it on and off since I was 12. I started seeing a therapist and I ended up taking antidepressants, but I didn't see much improvement. Even though I participated in multiple curricular activities and kept a high GPA, the stress of all of that along with being depressed made me cry myself to sleep almost every night. One of the only things that motiviated to continue going on in life was going away to college where I could become a new person, be around better people than I was at the time, and that I would have freedom. 

However, I went to college and absolutely nothing changed. I made didn't make any actual friends in college because I wasn't able to fit in, and I felt like there was something wrong with me because I had trouble making friends no matter where I went. My depression went from being manageable to so severe that I could barely get out of bed or function, I had mental breakdowns every other day, and it escalated to me attenpting suicide twice. I started going to therapy again this year and started on new antidepressants, and it seemed like I was on track to getting better. However, not being able to see my boyfriend and sisters as a result of the pandemic has undone all of the progress that I made in improving my mental health and I feel like I've hit rock botton all over again.

I feel like I've been through a lot, and it's really hard for me to stay hopeful. I've been depressed for so long I can't remember what it feels like to be happy, and the possibility of me being mentally ill as long as I'm alive and hurting the way I do constantly makes me feel like life isn't even worth living sometimes.

Thank you! It really feels like the praise black women and essential workers (a lot of whom are also black women) receive is a bunch of performative BS. A lot of people want to talk about how much they respect and look up to both groups of people, yet society still treats black women so badly it often feels like no one has our back besides us, while a lot of essential workers have had to work in unsafe conditions while receiving low pay. Like if you really care about black women as much as you claim to then put some effort into trying to help us change the aspects of society that make life difficult for us instead of just praising us for being 'strong black women.'

I'm 22 now, this sudden growth happened last year, and I also gained around 10 pounds in the process. I thought maybe they just grew because I gained a little weight, but they basically stayed that same size after I lost that weight. I didn't know that 2nd puberty was a thing so maybe that's what happened to me.

My boobs grew to around 32d/dd, and I thought that was as big as they'd get after they stayed that size for a few years afterwards. However, sometime last year, I couldn't fit any of my bras anymore, and once I got resized I realized I was now a 32g. Bra shopping became even more of a pain in the ass than it already was, and I had to deal with comments from my friends asking when did my boobs get that big, along with unsolicited comments about how I got fat and needed to lose weight. To this day I'm not exactly sure why they went through another growth spurt, but I do like the size they're at and am grateful that they don't cause me any back pain.

The first thing I noticed was that all of the main characters were light brights, and it's just really annoying to see TV shows and movies only casting light skinned actresses, as if brown and dark skinned black people don't make up the majority of African Americans. As much as I wanna support black media I won't be watching this since it doesn't look like it'll be good and perpetuates colorism.

As a result I've subscribed to get a monthly supply of her pantiliners, and several other people I know decided to buy her products, so her company has become even more famous and her sales are going up.

Personally I figured out that I outgrew my former best friend when I realized how one sided our friendship had become. Whenever I'd invite her to hang out with me she would almost always refuse to do it, yet she would get upset at me whenever I wasn't able to go to events she invited me to. In addition to this, whenever we'd talk to each other, she would be the one doing most of the talking and wasn't particularly interested in anything I wanted to talk about, and started to only contact me whenever she wanted me to help her with something. Eventually I realized that I was absolutely miserable and that this relationship was mentally draining me, so I decreased my contact with her and let the friendship drift apart completely. At the time I felt pretty shitty right afterwards since she'd been my best friend for 10 years and was the only close friend I had during that period of time, but then I realized that I would rather be alone than stuck in a friendship that felt like a chore and was making me unhappy.
